definition: A quantity that has magnitude (size) only, with no direction. Examples: speed, distance, mass, temperature, energy.
clues: This is a type of physical quantity
It has only size, not direction
Speed and mass are examples
A quantity with magnitude only — no direction; e.g. speed, distance, mass, temperature and energy are all scalars

definition: A quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Examples: velocity, displacement, force, acceleration, momentum.
clues: This is a type of physical quantity
It has both size and direction
Velocity and force are examples
A quantity with both magnitude and direction — e.g. velocity, displacement, force, acceleration and momentum are all vectors

definition: The distance travelled in a specific direction. A vector quantity measured in metres (m).
clues: This is a vector quantity
It is distance measured in a specific direction
Unlike distance, it can be negative
Distance in a stated direction — a vector version of distance; moving 5 m east and 5 m west gives a displacement of zero

definition: The speed of an object in a given direction. A vector quantity measured in m/s.
clues: This is a vector quantity
It is the vector equivalent of speed
It includes direction as well as magnitude
Speed in a stated direction — a vector; two objects can have the same speed but different velocities if moving in different directions

definition: A force that acts between objects that are physically touching, such as friction, tension, normal contact force or air resistance.
clues: This is a type of force
It requires physical contact between objects
Friction and tension are examples
A force that only acts when objects are touching — e.g. friction, tension, normal contact force, air resistance

definition: A force that acts between objects that are not touching, such as gravity, electrostatic force or magnetic force.
clues: This is a type of force
It acts between objects that are not touching
Gravity and magnetism are examples
A force that acts at a distance without contact — e.g. gravity, electrostatic force and magnetic force act through empty space

definition: The force of gravity acting on an object. W = mg. Measured in newtons (N). Depends on gravitational field strength.
clues: This is a force acting on all objects with mass
It is measured in newtons
It depends on where you are in the universe
The gravitational pull on an object — W = mg; it changes with gravitational field strength but mass stays constant

definition: The amount of matter in an object. Measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
clues: This is a property of all objects
It is measured in kilograms
It does not change with location
The amount of matter in an object — measured in kg; remains the same on Earth, the Moon or in space

definition: The force of gravity per unit mass at a point in a gravitational field. On Earth g ≈ 10 N/kg.
clues: This is a property of a gravitational field
It is measured in N/kg
On Earth it is approximately 10 N/kg
The gravitational force per kilogram of mass — g ≈ 10 N/kg on Earth; lower on the Moon (~1.6 N/kg)

definition: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting on an object combined. Found by adding forces as vectors.
clues: This is the net overall force on an object
It is found by combining all individual forces
It determines whether an object accelerates
The single equivalent force of all forces combined — if it is zero, the object is in equilibrium; if non-zero, the object accelerates

definition: When the resultant force on an object is zero — the object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
clues: This is a state of an object in physics
The resultant force on the object is zero
The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity
When all forces are balanced and the resultant force is zero — the object is stationary or moves in a straight line at constant speed

definition: The energy transferred when a force moves an object through a distance. W = Fs. Measured in joules (J).
clues: This is a concept linking force and distance
Energy is transferred when a force moves something
It is measured in joules
W = Fs — energy transferred when a force causes movement; 1 joule = 1 newton × 1 metre

definition: When an object returns to its original shape and size after the force is removed.
clues: This is a type of deformation
The object returns to its original shape when the force is removed
A spring returning to normal length is an example
Temporary deformation — the object returns to its original shape once the deforming force is removed; within the elastic limit

definition: When an object does not return to its original shape and size after the force is removed — permanently deformed.
clues: This is a type of deformation
The object does not return to its original shape
It is permanent
Permanent deformation — the material does not spring back after the force is removed; occurs beyond the elastic limit

definition: The extension of a spring is directly proportional to the force applied, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded. F = ke.
clues: This is a law relating force and extension in springs
Extension is proportional to force
It only applies up to a certain point
F = ke — force is proportional to extension while the elastic limit is not exceeded; the constant k is the spring constant

definition: A measure of the stiffness of a spring. The force needed to extend or compress it by 1 metre. Measured in N/m. Symbol: k.
clues: This is a property of a spring
It measures how stiff a spring is
It is measured in N/m
The stiffness of a spring — k = F/e; a high spring constant means more force is needed per metre of extension

definition: The maximum force beyond which a spring will not return to its original length — permanent deformation occurs.
clues: This is a threshold in spring/elastic behaviour
Beyond this point, the material is permanently deformed
Hooke's Law only applies below this point
The maximum force a spring can take and still return to its original length — beyond it, permanent deformation occurs

definition: A graph showing how the distance travelled by an object changes over time. The gradient gives the speed.
clues: This is a type of graph used in physics
It shows distance on the y-axis and time on the x-axis
The gradient tells you the speed
A graph of distance vs time — a straight line means constant speed; a steeper gradient means higher speed; a horizontal line means stationary

definition: A graph showing how the velocity of an object changes over time. Gradient gives acceleration; area under graph gives distance.
clues: This is a type of graph used in physics
It shows velocity on the y-axis and time on the x-axis
The gradient gives acceleration and the area gives distance
A graph of velocity vs time — gradient = acceleration; area under line = distance travelled; horizontal line = constant velocity

definition: The rate of change of velocity. a = (v - u) / t or F = ma. Measured in m/s². Can be positive (speeding up) or negative (decelerating).
clues: This is a quantity in physics measured in m/s²
It describes how quickly velocity changes
It can be positive or negative
The rate of change of velocity — a = (v−u)/t; positive means speeding up, negative means slowing down (deceleration)

definition: An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a resultant force. Objects resist changes in motion.
clues: This is one of three laws of motion
It describes what happens when no resultant force acts
Objects resist changes in their state of motion
An object stays still or moves at constant velocity unless a resultant force acts — it resists any change in its motion

definition: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the resultant force and inversely proportional to its mass. F = ma.
clues: This is one of three laws of motion
It relates force, mass and acceleration
Its equation is F = ma
The resultant force equals mass times acceleration — F = ma; greater force or less mass gives greater acceleration

definition: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always act in pairs on different objects.
clues: This is one of three laws of motion
It describes forces acting in pairs
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Forces always come in equal and opposite pairs acting on different objects — e.g. a rocket pushes gas backwards, the gas pushes the rocket forwards

definition: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. Related to its mass.
clues: This is a property of objects
It describes resistance to changes in motion
Heavier objects have more of this
The tendency to resist changes in motion — the more mass an object has, the harder it is to start, stop or change its direction

definition: The distance a vehicle travels during the driver's reaction time before braking begins.
clues: This is part of the stopping distance of a vehicle
It is the distance covered before braking starts
It depends on reaction time and speed
The distance a car travels while the driver reacts — affected by speed, tiredness, alcohol and drugs

definition: The distance a vehicle travels after braking until it stops. Depends on speed, braking force, road conditions and tyre condition.
clues: This is part of the stopping distance of a vehicle
It is the distance covered while braking
It depends on road conditions and speed
The distance a vehicle travels from when brakes are applied until it stops — affected by speed, road grip, tyre condition and brake quality

definition: The total distance needed to stop a vehicle. Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance.
clues: This is the total distance to stop a vehicle
It is the sum of two other distances
It increases significantly with speed
Thinking distance + braking distance — the total distance from perceiving a hazard to coming to a complete stop

definition: The product of an object's mass and velocity. p = mv. Measured in kg m/s. A vector quantity.
clues: This is a vector quantity in physics
It is the product of mass and velocity
It is measured in kg m/s
p = mv — a vector quantity; a heavy, fast-moving object has much more of this than a light, slow one

definition: The total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after, provided no external forces act.
clues: This is a law in physics
It applies to collisions and explosions
The total momentum before and after is the same
In a closed system, total momentum is unchanged by collisions — m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂

definition: The change in momentum of an object. Impulse = force × time = Δp. Measured in N s or kg m/s.
clues: This is a quantity related to momentum
It equals force multiplied by time
It equals the change in momentum
Impulse = FΔt = Δp — the longer a force acts, the greater the change in momentum; crumple zones extend impact time to reduce force
